candidates.attacker_control: Remote, unauthenticated HTTP request to any mapping of this servlet, e.g. GET /ResourceServlet?resource=/WEB-INF/web.xml or ...?resource=../<path> (the value is also splittable on ',', ';', whitespace via RESOURCE_URL_DELIMITERS, line 277).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether a guard exists: allowedResources (line 280) is optional (null by default) and matches the unnormalized token, so patterns using '**' can still be satisfied by '..' segments; no cleanPath/isInvalidPath equivalent is present in this class. Checked the non-deprecated handler (ResourceHttpRequestHandler/PathResourceResolver) - its checks are real but are not inherited by ResourceServlet. Checked for callers/tests: no test or in-repo caller references ResourceServlet, i.e. this is legacy-configuration dependent, and container RequestDispatcher normalization may limit filesystem escapes, so impact is container/config dependent. No runtime or container testing was performed.
candidates.impact: Server-side path traversal / unauthorized resource inclusion: protected web-app content that clients cannot normally address (e.g. /WEB-INF/*.jsp views, WEB-INF/web.xml, classpath properties exposed through the context) can be included into the attacker's response; JSP targets are executed by the container, so protected view logic or data can be rendered to the attacker. On containers whose dispatcher resolves '..' segments beyond the mapping/context root, the traversal can reach resources outside the intended static root, giving confidential file disclosure. This is the class of issue the project addressed for this servlet in the 4.3.5/4.2.9 maintenance releases.
candidates.prerequisites: Application still uses (or is configured with) the deprecated ResourceServlet, which is the legacy alternative to ResourceHttpRequestHandler; the servlet container must resolve the dispatcher path (include) to web-app-internal or parent resources. ResourceServlet itself documents that with allowedResources unset 'any target resource can be requested, including resources in the WEB-INF directory' (lines 53-56).
candidates.root_cause: org.springframework.web.servlet.ResourceServlet (deprecated as of 4.3.5) derives the target path verbatim from the attacker-controlled HTTP parameter "resource" (determineResourceUrl, line 240-242) and passes each token straight to the servlet container: request.getRequestDispatcher(url).include(request, response) (doInclude, lines 270-290). There is no normalization or denylist for "..", absolute/context-escaping paths, or URL-scheme prefixes. The only constraint is the optional allowedResources Ant pattern, which is null by default and is matched against the raw, unnormalized token, so it does not stop traversal segments.
candidates.title: Unvalidated 'resource' parameter in deprecated ResourceServlet lets remote users traverse to/ include protected web-app resources
candidates.trace: doGet (line 196) -> determineResourceUrl (240) returns request.getParameter("resource") -> doInclude (270) -> optional allowedResources Ant match (280) -> request.getRequestDispatcher(url).include(request, response) (287-288). Nothing canonicalizes or rejects traversal, WEB-INF/META-INF segments, or scheme-looking values; contrast with the guard implemented for the non-deprecated handler in ResourceHttpRequestHandler.isInvalidPath (lines 480-509) and PathResourceResolver.isResourceUnderLocation (160-204), which this servlet does not use. getFileTimestamp (332-348) likewise feeds the raw value into ServletContextResource.
candidates.unverified: The exact upstream fix diff is not available in this snapshot, so the intended ground-truth file/lines could not be confirmed; whether Tomcat/Jetty normalize dispatcher paths enough to fully block '..' escapes was not runtime-tested. The 4.3.5-cycle alignment (version string, issue references, '@since 4.3.5' markers) is the basis for treating this path as the snapshot's target issue.
candidates.weakness_type: Path traversal / unsafe server-side include (CWE-22; server-side file inclusion of WEB-INF content)

coverage_summary: Scope: the full assigned tree of 7,264 model-visible files (6,391 Java, ~37 MB) across all 22 modules; 1 file excluded by sensitive-name/path filter and binary-like files skipped by policy. I inspected in depth: spring-webmvc resource handling (ResourceServlet, ResourceHttpRequestHandler, PathResourceResolver), spring-messaging/spring-websocket STOMP selector and broker flow, spring-context/spring-web remoting serialization paths, spring-beans/spring-context data binding and auto-grow limits, spring-core StringUtils/cleanPath, and the associated test trees. The P1 relation index is partial (34 parsed files of 7,264 files indexed with cross-file edges, 395 omitted files, 181,823 unresolved calls, no control- or data-flow analysis and no semantic resolution), so it was used only for navigation; every candidate above was verified against source text. Remaining areas (spring-jdbc, spring-orm, spring-jms, spring-oxm, spring-test, portlet/tiles modules) were only sampled, not exhaustively audited.
limitations: No upstream git history, fix commit, or patch is available in the snapshot, so the dataset's ground-truth file/lines could not be positively confirmed; the identification rests on version/issue-date alignment (4.3.5.BUILD-SNAPSHOT, December 2016).
No code execution, container testing, or exploit payloads were permitted/used; container-specific RequestDispatcher path normalization and allowedResources bypass behavior remain unverified.

The P1 relation index provides syntax-level navigation only (partial indexing, no data-flow/reachability), and 181,823 calls were unresolved, so undiscovered vulnerabilities may remain in uninspected modules.

Only one candidate may be submitted; other plausible leads (STOMP selector SpEL, HttpInvoker deserialization, binding-related root cause) were deliberately not submitted and are not runtime-confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-controlled SpEL in STOMP subscription selector: spring-messaging DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.addSubscriptionInternal parses the attacker-supplied 'selector' native header with a plain SpelExpressionParser (lines 144-148) and filterSubscriptions evaluates it against StandardEvaluationContext(message) (lines 211-216) with no restriction on type references/constructors/method invocation. A STOMP client that can SUBSCRIBE over WebSocket and cause a message to that destination could achieve code execution (the pattern fixed years later as CVE-2018-1270).
rejected_leads.reason: Real and high impact, but this snapshot's version (4.3.5.BUILD-SNAPSHOT, December 2016) does not match that issue's later fix window (4.3.15, April 2018); with a one-candidate cap it is recorded as an unconfirmed alternate rather than a second candidate. Reachability also requires an app that enables the STOMP simple broker.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe Java deserialization in Spring remoting (HttpInvoker / RemoteInvocationSerializingExporter): createObjectInputStream returns CodebaseAwareObjectInputStream and doReadRemoteInvocation calls readObject() before any type check (spring-context .../remoting/rmi/RemoteInvocationSerializingExporter.java lines 122-145; HttpInvokerServiceExporter in spring-web).
rejected_leads.reason: Legitimate RCE surface if an application exposes the deprecated HTTP-invoker exporter, but it is an inherent design property of the remoting endpoints (no upstream whitelist exists in this codebase) and it is not localized to a single snapshot-specific fix, so it is weaker as the intended finding.

rejected_leads.lead: Data-binding reachability of class/classLoader properties (root cause later used by CVE-2022-22965): CachedIntrospectionResults/BeanWrapperImpl in spring-beans expose nested properties such as class.* and classLoader.* to WebDataBinder-driven request-parameter binding.
rejected_leads.reason: Present code pattern but exploitation depends on environment (JDK 9+, servlet container/WAR specifics) and on a diffuse root cause; no snapshot-specific validation gap could be pinpointed to a single location, so it was not selected.

summary: Reviewed the Spring Framework 4.3.5.BUILD-SNAPSHOT tree (7,264 model-visible files, 6,391 Java) with emphasis on web/resource handling, remoting serialization, messaging/STOMP expression use, and beans data binding. The version string dates the snapshot to the December 2016 4.3.5 development window (no 2017 copyrights; newest issue references SPR-15009/SPR-15015; all \"@since 4.3.5\" markers present), i.e. the fix window for the path-traversal issue in the legacy ResourceServlet. That class still ships raw attacker input to a RequestDispatcher include with no path validation, which is the single best-supported candidate. A second, higher-impact issue (client-controlled SpEL in spring-messaging's STOMP subscription selector) is also present in-tree but its public fix window (4.3.15, April 2018) does not match this snapshot, so it is recorded as an unconfirmed rejected lead rather than a second candidate.
